title: The Monthly Fee Isn't the Cost. The Decisions Made Without One Are.
linkedin:
Most owners size up a fractional CFO against one number: the monthly fee.

That's the wrong comparison.

Here's the pattern we see across owner-led businesses: the fee is concrete. It has a dollar figure, it lands on the same date each month, and it's easy to weigh against what the business paid before that line existed.

The cost of operating without that function is structured completely differently. It's a pricing decision that holds on gut feel eighteen months longer than it should. A cash gap spotted the week it bites instead of the quarter before. A loan application that takes three attempts because the numbers behind it were pulled together in a hurry.

None of that gets labelled "the cost of not having financial oversight." It gets absorbed into the general feeling that the year was tougher than it needed to be.

Add those costs up over twelve months and the total is very often larger than a year of fractional CFO fees would have been. The reason owners rarely make that comparison isn't that the numbers don't support it. It's that the fee is one visible number, while the alternative cost is scattered across a dozen small decisions nobody ever totals.

The better starting question isn't "can I afford this fee." It's "what have the quiet decisions already cost this year."

Full piece on the ProfitPulse blog.

Quick question for business owners: have you ever added up what a "quiet" year actually cost you?

Not the big disasters, the small stuff. A price that didn't move when it should have. A cash gap you spotted a week too late. A loan application that took three goes because the numbers weren't ready.

Most owners never total that up, so it never gets compared to anything. But add those small decisions together over twelve months and the number is often bigger than people expect.
